newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha steady in quiet market, crude supports.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha steady in quiet market, crude supports.

text.p: NWE naphtha was steady on Wednesday in quiet trade as Brent futures lent some support, traders said.
May swaps were assessed at around $181/181.50, while June was talked 50 cents to $1.0 above there.
Traders said the north European market remained on the slack side, although dribs and drabs were being worked to Asia which was expected to keep the Mediterranean on the tight side.
On the cargo front, bids for pipeline spec cargoes were seen around the $180 cif NWE mark.
Barge size parcels were valued around the low $171s.
Traders said they had seen some interest out of the U.S. Gulf although it was not clear if anything had actually been done in that direction.

"Last week's sell-off left NWE naphtha the cheapest around so it's not surprising to see people trying to work the arb," said one trader. "But if cargoes get back into the mid-$180s range these opportunities will soon close." -- Melanie Goodfellow, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714.
